They take place on the threshold between our daily world and a mysteriously unknown realm. Now, many movies and books cross this threshold merely to scare the bejeezus out of us. But the greatest ghost stories aim to do something more — such as capturing the weight of Mexico's past like Juan Rulfo's Pedro Páramo , or exploring one's own madness, as Stanley Kubrick does in his adaptation of Stephen King 's much saner The Shining . You find that brand of ambition in My Sad Dead , a new Spanish-language Netflix series centering on a woman who can see and talk to ghosts. items.text: Met Office issues October snow verdict as temperatures to drop across UK
items.article: The mercury hit 26.3C in Cambridge on Wednesday as most of the country experienced sunny conditions — but the unseasonal warmth won't last, Met Office forecasters say The Met Office has delivered its assessment on the likelihood of snow descending on the UK this October. Britain enjoyed a string of sweltering heatwaves throughout the summer, with temperatures frequently surpassing 35C and a number of records tumbling in the process. Temperatures have been steadily dropping over the past fortnight, with glorious sunshine giving way to heavier downpours and bitter, gusting winds. Despite this, Met Office forecasters have told said there are currently "no strong signals for widespread or disruptive snowfall across the UK during October". The meteorologists do, though, understand temperatures will drop in the coming days — to as low as 10C in the daytime. This is below the average for October and a plunge from the balmy weather the UK has experienced this week. A high of 26.3C was recorded in Cambridge on Wednesday. Holbeach in Lincolnshire saw the mercury reach 25.7C, while 24.9C was noted near Heathrow Airport in west London. But now brief cold snaps have not been entirely ruled out, with the higher reaches of Scotland considered the most probable locations to experience snow should wintry conditions take hold.

Certain investments — such as private equity funds, venture capital and hedge funds, among others — commonly require investors to be accredited to participate. items.text: Eon given the green light to buy Ovo - what does it mean for customers?
items.article: Six energy businesses currently hold more than 90% of the UK's household energy market. This is going down to five. German energy provider Eon has been given the green light to buy UK firm Ovo and create one of the country's largest energy suppliers. The competition regulator today waved through Eon's bid in the latest sign of consolidation in the energy sector as the number of main suppliers falls to five. Eon has about 5.6million customers in the UK. Once it acquires Ovo, the combined group's customer base is expected to be around 9.6million, potentially making it the largest energy provider in the UK. Earlier this year, Eon boss Chris Norbury said greater scale would allow the combined group to improve the range of products and help bring energy bills down. The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) today said that the deal would not reduce competition in the market. But when energy bills are forecast to soar, and the number of suppliers is falling, should customers be worried?
